newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 18.

text.p: A Nihon Keizai Shimbun survey of 445 venture capital businesses showed that 85 percent of them want to list their shares on stock exchanges, while 46 percent of the companies established since 1990 also hope to go public within five years. The respondents said they expect their sales to grow by an average of more than 18 percent for the year ending on March, 31, with current profit jumping by an average more than 56 percent.

Nomura Securities Co Ltd will become the first Japanese securities company in Moscow when it sets up an office next year. Nomura's British unit plans to be a lead-manager for a Euro-dollar bond to be issued by the city of Moscow in February. Nomura is expected to issue $300 to $500 million worth of Eurobonds in Russia.

Leading life insurance companies are expanding purchases of bonds denominated in foreign currencies as they expect the dollar to stay close to its current level of 110 yen. Meiji Life Insurance Co Ltd plans to purchase about 200 billion yen worth of such bonds, while Dai-Ichi Life Insurance Co Ltd will increase its investments by more than 100 billion yen in the second half year to March 1997.
The world's third-largest telecommunications company, Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG, will list its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
